defects.before: `PROSE` collects the visible text of the page for the word count.
defects.after: `PROSE` collects the prose of the page for the word count. The comment names what is not counted: tables, captions, the word list and the references.
defects.evidence: The comment of line 39 says "visible prose outside tables, captions, word list and references", so not all visible text is collected.

defects.after: One `Rg` object for each of 15 record groups.
defects.evidence: Lines 463 to 469 build 15 ranges, and the groups `A_NEW`, `C_READ`, `C_ASM` and `C_ASM_FI` get no range there.

defects.before: Two ranges that share exactly one value count as overlapping.
defects.after: Two ranges that share exactly one value count as overlapping. The test uses the rates as `val` returns them (6 decimals for a bwx record), not the rounded text.
defects.evidence: `overlaps` (line 208) compares `lo` and `hi`, which are the `Decimal` values of `val` (line 188 keeps 6 decimals), and the unit instructions ask how values are rounded and compared.

defects.before: One call takes either part A records or bwx records, never both.
defects.after: The script stops when one call mixes part A records and bwx records.
defects.evidence: Line 365 is a `need` call that stops the build on a mix, and the old sentence did not say that the script stops.

defects.before: The drop is computed between the two medians, so between the middle interval of each process.
defects.after:
(text changed to 5 bullets) ... - The drop is computed between the two medians. With 3 intervals the median is the middle one of the 3 rates. It is not always the second interval in time.
- Example: in session 1, round 1 the 3 rates of `bw_old` are 467.83, 467.92 and 465.38 GB/s in time order. The median is 467.83 GB/s, the first interval [Ref3].
defects.evidence: "Middle interval" reads as the second interval in time, but lines 4 to 6 of k120-T72A1-20261117T221209Z/threads120.csv hold 467.83, 467.92, 465.38 GB/s and the sandbox run of lines 1 to 568 gives the median 467.83 (interval 0).

defects.after: `facts_data.py` adds in the same order, and `build_facts.py` (named in the comment of lines 177 to 181) takes its sum from there.
defects.evidence: The docstring at the left names build_facts.py while the text named facts_data.py; facts_data.py lines 361 to 374 hold the sum and build_facts.py line 153 takes `iv['total']` from `fd.bwx_intervals`.

defects.before: Rounds the lowest and the highest drop of the list to 0.1 with `f1`.
defects.after: Rounds the lowest and the highest drop of the list to 0.1 % with `f1`.
defects.evidence: The number had no unit; the drops are percent values (line 418 multiplies by 100).

defects.before: The page is written at the end of the file, so a stop leaves the page on disk as it was.
defects.after: The page is written only at the end of the file. So a stop leaves the page on disk as it was.
defects.evidence: Two claims in one sentence; `OUT` is opened only in line 2829, which supports the word "only".

defects.before: The comment gives the reason: the two input files are rebuilt from time to time, so a read can find a file that is only partly written.
defects.after: The comment gives the reason: another agent rebuilds the two input files from time to time, and a read can then find a file that is only partly written.
defects.evidence: Two claims were joined with ", so"; the docstring of line 65 names another agent as the one that rebuilds the files.

defects.before: A byte that is not valid UTF-8 is replaced by a replacement character, so the read does not fail on it.
defects.after: A byte that is not valid UTF-8 is replaced by a replacement character. So the read does not fail on such a byte.
defects.evidence: Two claims in one sentence (rule: one claim per sentence).

defects.evidence: Two claims in one sentence (rule: one claim per sentence).

defects.after: A csv file of that runner holds several processes. So the rows are taken by their place in the file.

defects.before: The end of the file prints the list and writes the page only when every line passed.
defects.after: The end of the file prints the list. It writes the page only when every line passed.
defects.evidence: Lines 2820 to 2830 of make_report.py print every line of CHECKS in all cases and open OUT only when no check failed, so the joined sentence could be read as "the list is printed only when every line passed".

defects.before:
- `r7`: the range of the 3 intervals of session 1, which are 1 process.
- `r8`: the range of the 6 intervals of A-1 and A-2 of the same round, which are 2 processes.
- The script stops unless `r7` lies fully above `r8`. `near` is the distance of the nearest ends.
defects.after:
- `r7`: the range of the intervals of session 1. `r8`: the range of the intervals of A-1 and A-2 of the same round.
- Line 513: the script stops unless `r7` holds 3 intervals of 1 process and `r8` holds 6 intervals of 2 processes.
- Line 514: the script stops unless `r7` lies fully above `r8`. `near` is the distance of the nearest ends.
defects.evidence: Line 513 is a hard assertion `need(r7.n == 3 and r7.np == 1 and r8.n == 6 and r8.np == 2, ...)` that stops the build, and the old text gave these counts as facts without saying that a wrong count stops the script.

defects.before: `_FILES` keeps the lines of every csv file that was read. [...] So each csv file is read from disk only once.
defects.after: `_FILES` keeps the lines of every csv file that `file_lines` has read. [...] So `file_lines` reads each csv file from disk only once.
defects.evidence: Lines 1209 to 1213 of make_report.py open every `.csv` file under `R` a second time without `_FILES` (for example a6456.csv of T72L1), and lines 1353, 1373 and 1456 read one-thread.csv, A5.csv and A6.csv with `lines_of` directly, so the count "only once" held only for reads through `file_lines` (line 120).

defects.before: - The printed rate is only compared. The page value is the sum of the T rows.
defects.after: - In these lines the printed rate is only compared. The page value is the sum of the T rows.
defects.evidence: `grep -n "i_row_rate(" make_report.py` gives a third caller in line 1430, which writes the printed rate of the record `LOWEST_ASM` into a reference entry, and the built page holds "Its interval row prints 288.53 GB/s" once.
